text:
anya: Heads up — CI perf alert for eu-west L4 pool after the release window. p95 token latency for small-chat workload jumped ~35% on L4 nodes only. Not seeing same on H100s.

devin: saw the same in staging-2. Queue depth and batching metrics look normal but kernel-selection logs show frequent fallback to the generic matmul path around step 0-16. Could be causing extra memcpy.

mike: any noisy-neighbor events on those hosts? nvlink/rdma errors? sre-ops can you check cloud-side telemetry?

sre-ops: checked host-level: no obvious noisy-tenant CPU spike. Network counters show increased retransmits on eth0 for a subset of hosts in eu-west-2 (~5 hosts). Not across the whole pool.

anya: attaching profiler snippet (from a failing run):
```
[profile] timeline: kernel_select:generic_matmul 60.3%
[profile] timeline: kernel_select:optimized_mha 2.1%
[profile] memcpy: 18.7%
[profile] rdma_wait: 9.4%
[profile] batching_wait: 3.2%
```

devin: that matches my trace. We expect optimized kernels for 128/1 and 256/2 sequences, but something is forcing generic path. Suspect recent kernel selector heuristics change in commit 3a7f9b0 (PR #3418) that relaxed the tensor-alignment check.

mike: if kernel selection falls back we do extra allocations and memcpy which amplifies network jitter. On L4 the optimized kernel had an inline RDMA-friendly path; generic_matmul goes through staging buffers.

perf-ci-bot: CI perf job eu-west/L4/small-chat: baseline median latency 72ms, current run median 98ms, p95 210ms -> 285ms (+35%). Related CI runs: eu-west/H100 unchanged.

anya: can someone bisect on 3a7f9b0..3b20c1a to confirm? If it's that heuristic, we need a revert or quick-fix to force selection on L4.

devin: running a local bisect now — will try toggling the new alignment flag and also force-kernel=optimized for the model.

sre-ops: I marked the 5 hosts as quarantined and shifted traffic. New runs on healthy hosts show p95 back to ~220ms for same model (so still slightly higher than baseline, but much better than 285ms).

mike: reproducer config I used: 
```
model: chat-medium
seq_len: 128
batch_policy: max_tokens=2048, prefer_small_batches=true
kernel_select: auto
force_kernel: none
```
Changing kernel_select to prefer_optimized brought p95 down ~12%.

devin: bisect result: 3b0f2a1 (part of PR #3418 split) is the culprit — it introduced a conservative fallback when alignment mismatch < 8 bytes, but logic incorrectly triggers for certain L4 memory layouts. Patch queued: revert that chunk and add explicit L4 exception.

anya: thanks. Action items: (1) devin push revert branch and roll a canary to eu-west L4 only, (2) mike add a guard in kernel selector to log fallback reason (align/shape/quant), (3) sre-ops keep hosts quarantined until canary stabilizes, (4) perf team add a small synthetic to CI that exercises the L4 memcpy-heavy path so we catch this earlier.

devin: working on revert branch now — will link PR when ready. Expect canary in ~30m.

mike: also posting a short runbook note in #eng-runtime-runbooks about how to force optimized kernel and diagnose RDMA retransmits.

perf-ci-bot: New canary job kicked off: eu-west/L4/canary-3b0f2a1-revert. Monitoring p95 and rdma retransmits.

anya: great — keep updates here. If revert fixes, we'll schedule a full revert and follow-up with a corrected heuristic and more unit tests. :thumbsup:
